days.theme: Half-day arrival — the river hill before dinner, the lit lakes after it
days.why: Work backwards from the boat, which is the only thing here with a real clock on it. Train clears ~14:50, transfer downtown is the stated ~45 min, so you are at the hotel ~15:40 and out again by ~16:15 with bags gone. Elephant Trunk Hill takes the 16:45–17:30 slot: it is 200 m from the hotel, it is the city's signature karst shape, and it is free from the riverside promenade / Love Island viewpoint — no ticket queue, no commitment. That leaves the gap before sunset (~19:05) for dinner and an unhurried wander of the Zhengyang pedestrian streets, which are right there and cost nothing to add. Then Two Rivers & Four Lakes as the night event, boarding ~20:00 for the 90-minute illuminated loop past the Sun & Moon Twin Pagodas on Shanhu Lake — the run operates 19:00–21:30 (extended 18:00–23:00 June–October, so late August is comfortable) with boats every 10–30 minutes, meaning a missed connection earlier in the day costs you nothing. Two stops is the honest answer for this afternoon: both are central, neither is rushed, and there is real slack absorbing a late train.
days.load_note: 135 min stop time (2.25 h) across a ~15:40–21:30 window. Light by design — a 45-minute transfer, a check-in and two meals eat most of an afternoon that only starts at 14:50, and the station is unconfirmed.

ideas.name: Reed Flute Cave
ideas.why: Does not fit and should not be forced. It closes at 18:00 (Apr 1–Oct 31 07:30–18:00) with last guided entry ~30 min before, and it is out of town to the northwest. Even the optimistic line — clear the station 14:50, straight there without checking in, 75 min inside — lands you back downtown around 17:00 having dragged luggage to a cave, and it only works at all from Guilin North (~3.5 km away). If the arrival is actually Guilin West, it is ~20 km further and the maths collapses entirely. The sight's own note already says to skip it in favour of the stronger Silver Cave later in the trip — take that advice. Keep it as a wet-weather substitute only if a later Guilin morning materialises.

ideas.name: Check in at RongShi
ideas.why: Not a sight — logistics, kept out of the stop list per the no-hotels rule. Budget 30 min around 15:40, on the cruise-wharf side of downtown, which is why both real stops are within walking distance of it.

notes: Which Guilin station you arrive at is still unconfirmed and it changes the afternoon materially: Guilin North is ~15 km / ~30–45 min from downtown, Guilin West is ~20 km further southwest and closer to an hour. The plan is built so that either works — nothing before 20:00 is time-critical. Confirm the station before considering any additions.

Two Rivers & Four Lakes runs 19:00–21:30 normally, extended to 18:00–23:00 June–October, departures every 10–30 min, ~1.5 h for the full two-rivers loop (the four-lakes-only round trip is ~1 h). No advance booking strictly needed, but the lights and the pagodas are the whole point so do not take a departure before ~19:45.
Sunset in Guilin on 29 August is ~19:05. Elephant Trunk Hill is worth seeing in daylight, which is exactly why it goes before dinner and not after.

Reed Flute Cave hours vary by source (07:30–18:00 April–October is the most commonly listed; some list 08:00–17:30 for July–December). Either way it is closed by the time this afternoon could realistically reach it.

If the train runs early or the arrival station turns out to be Guilin North, the natural addition is not Reed Flute Cave but Fubo Hill or Solitary Beauty Peak — both central, both a 45-minute climb, both slotting into the 17:45–18:45 gap without touching the boat.
